transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because things have gotten a bit out of hand lately. What finally made me realize I needed to talk to someone is... well, after I eat too much, I've started going upstairs and making myself throw up. Then I just come back down and act like nothing happened, like I was just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed. It's just become this routine that I can't seem to stop.
Would you say that your current body weight is significantly lower than what is healthy for you?

Well, I don't really see it that way myself. But... my daughter, and actually a woman from my church, have both told me recently that I look too thin. 

So maybe I am. It's just... I still panic if my skirt feels even a little snug when I put it on for work, or if the scale goes up by just one pound. When that happens, I feel like I’ve somehow let myself become huge overnight, no matter what anyone else says.
When you eat too much, do you feel unable to control your eating?

Yes, I really do. It's... well, once I start, it feels like a switch just flips. It's almost like I'm watching myself keep eating, and there's a part of me in my head saying, 'Linda, stop now,' but I just can't. My hands just keep reaching for more food, no matter what I tell myself.
Do you deliberately restrict how much you eat in order to prevent gaining weight?

Yes, I do. Usually, if I've had one of those episodes, the next day I’ll just skip breakfast and lunch entirely. Or I'll push myself to do extra laps with my walking group. It's not because I feel energetic or want the extra exercise... it's really just because I’m trying to undo what I ate.
Has a medical professional told you that your current weight is significantly below what is healthy for your height?
No, I haven't been told that by a doctor. I actually haven't been to see my regular doctor in a while, so we haven't discussed my weight or anything like that.
What are your current height and weight?
I'm about 5 foot 4, and I weigh around 140 pounds.
How often, on average, have you been having these episodes of overeating followed by vomiting or other efforts to compensate?

Well, since last winter, um... I'd say there has hardly been a week when I haven’t had at least one of those private eating spells. And then, you know, I try to make up for it right after by throwing up, or skipping meals, or overdoing my walking like I mentioned.
